method: Explicit Grade 8 worked-example anchors and original numeric tables for the existing Rich V2 table renderer; no publisher pixels, graph renderer or automatic grading added.

visuals.Title: Triangle translated right four and up two
visuals.Description: Original rigid-motion table: translate every point by (4,2). All corresponding distances and angles must stay invariant. This table is not an interactive coordinate-grid construction.

visuals.Title: Translation left three and up two
visuals.Description: Original rigid-motion table: translate every point by (-3,2). All corresponding distances and angles must stay invariant. This table is not an interactive coordinate-grid construction.

visuals.Title: Triangle translated right four and down three
visuals.Description: Original rigid-motion table: translate every point by (4,-3). All corresponding distances and angles must stay invariant. This table is not an interactive coordinate-grid construction.

visuals.Title: Quadrilateral translated two units
visuals.Description: Original rigid-motion table: translate every point by (2,0). All corresponding distances and angles must stay invariant. This table is not an interactive coordinate-grid construction.

visuals.Title: Coordinate-axis reflection comparisons
visuals.Description: Original P=(3,2); reflecting over the x-axis changes only y, and reflecting over the y-axis changes only x.

visuals.Title: Order matters for compositions
visuals.Description: Starting at (1,1), translation by (2,0) then reflection in y-axis ends at (−3,1); the reverse order ends at (1,1).

visuals.Title: Parallel lines after translation
visuals.Description: Moving both horizontal lines two units up preserves their parallel nature.

visuals.Title: Circular grid distances at scale 2
visuals.Description: Multiply each distance from the dilation center by 2; rays are unchanged.

visuals.Title: Origin-centered dilations in coordinates
visuals.Description: For k positive, both coordinates multiply by the same factor, including negative coordinates.

visuals.Title: Dilation scales area by k²
visuals.Description: A 2 by 3 rectangle dilated by k=2 becomes 4 by 6; its area goes from 6 to 24.

visuals.Title: Line with slope two
visuals.Description: Original lesson-example input-output table. Each row uses y = 2x + 0. Plotting this relation, when required, is a separate graphical task.

visuals.Title: Line through two given points
visuals.Description: Original lesson-example input-output table. Each row uses y = 2x + 1. Plotting this relation, when required, is a separate graphical task.

visuals.Title: Remaining water at constant loss rate
visuals.Description: Original lesson-example input-output table. Each row uses y = -2x + 30. Plotting this relation, when required, is a separate graphical task.

visuals.Title: Proportional input-output relationship
visuals.Description: Original lesson-example input-output table. Each row uses y = 3x + 0. Plotting this relation, when required, is a separate graphical task.

visuals.Title: Distance as a function of time
visuals.Description: Original lesson-example input-output table. Each row uses y = 4x + 0. Plotting this relation, when required, is a separate graphical task.

visuals.Title: Linear but not proportional
visuals.Description: Original lesson-example input-output table. Each row uses y = 3x + 4. Plotting this relation, when required, is a separate graphical task.

visuals.Title: Trip cost with a fixed fee
visuals.Description: Original lesson-example input-output table. Each row uses y = 2x + 6. Plotting this relation, when required, is a separate graphical task.

visuals.Title: Decreasing height with negative slope
visuals.Description: Original lesson-example input-output table. Each row uses y = -4x + 20. Plotting this relation, when required, is a separate graphical task.

visuals.Title: Rise and run on a line with slope two
visuals.Description: Original lesson-example input-output table. Each row uses y = 2x + 0. Plotting this relation, when required, is a separate graphical task.

visuals.Title: Ordered pairs on a two-variable line
visuals.Description: All listed points satisfy 2x+3y=12. A complete coordinate graph remains a separate task.

visuals.Title: Which candidate balances 2x+3=11?
visuals.Description: A solution has equal left and right sides; x=4 is the only solution shown.

visuals.Title: Variables on both sides
visuals.Description: The two expressions equal each other only when x=4 among the candidates shown.

visuals.Title: Identity versus contradiction
visuals.Description: The first equation is true for all real x; the second equation 2x+1=2x+5 is never true.

visuals.Title: Find the break-even month
visuals.Description: Plan A=6+3m; plan B=18+m. They have equal price at month 6.

visuals.Title: Intersection of two lines
visuals.Description: For the same x, both y-values agree at (2,3). A graph must be represented separately.

visuals.Title: Parallel and distinct equations
visuals.Description: Two lines with slope 2 and different intercepts never intersect.

visuals.Title: Check both parts of a system
visuals.Description: Only (3,7) satisfies y=2x+1 and x+y=10 in these choices.

visuals.Title: Check the difference constraint
visuals.Description: All listed pairs sum to 7, but only (4,3) also has x−y=1.

visuals.Title: Check a two-price fruit system
visuals.Description: Eight fruits total; apples cost $2, pears $3. Five apples and three pears cost $19.

visuals.Title: Inputs and outputs of f(x)=2x+1
visuals.Description: Original lesson-example input-output table. Each row uses y = 2x + 1. Plotting this relation, when required, is a separate graphical task.

visuals.Title: Evaluation of a linear function
visuals.Description: Original lesson-example input-output table. Each row uses y = 2x − 5. Plotting this relation, when required, is a separate graphical task.

visuals.Title: Quadratic values are not linear
visuals.Description: Opposite inputs share the same square. Plotting the curve remains a separate graphic task.

visuals.Title: A fixed term plus rate
visuals.Description: Original lesson-example input-output table. Each row uses y = 2x + 5. Plotting this relation, when required, is a separate graphical task.

visuals.Title: A linear function with constant rate
visuals.Description: Original lesson-example input-output table. Each row uses y = 3x + 2. Plotting this relation, when required, is a separate graphical task.

visuals.Title: Two parts of one function
visuals.Description: Rule 2t applies for 0≤t≤2; rule 4 applies for 2<t≤4. No jump occurs at t=2.

visuals.Title: Volume and height in a right prism
visuals.Description: Height is volume divided by constant base area 20 cm².

visuals.Title: Cylinder volume and height
visuals.Description: For fixed radius 3, V=9πh, so the table shows the exact coefficient V/π.

visuals.Title: Sphere volume proportional to radius cubed
visuals.Description: V=(4/3)πr³. The table shows exact volume coefficients, not decimals.

visuals.Title: Cylinder water volume as height rises
visuals.Description: With fixed radius 2, water volume V=4πh.

visuals.Title: Line prediction and residual
visuals.Description: At x=4, the fit y=2x+2 predicts 10; observed 11 gives residual +1.

visuals.Title: A negative linear trend
visuals.Description: Original lesson-example input-output table. Each row uses y = -2x + 10. Plotting this relation, when required, is a separate graphical task.

visuals.Title: U-shaped nonlinear association
visuals.Description: The squared-input data do not have constant first differences.

visuals.Title: Rate of increase between two observations
visuals.Description: Original lesson-example input-output table. Each row uses y = 1.5x + 1.5. Plotting this relation, when required, is a separate graphical task.

visuals.Title: Conditional percentage of a group
visuals.Description: Divide by the full group count 20, not by another category.

visuals.Title: Multiply powers of ten
visuals.Description: Original exponent evaluation table. The nonzero base is 10; negative powers mean reciprocals, never a logarithm approximation.

visuals.Title: Divide powers of ten
visuals.Description: Original exponent evaluation table. The nonzero base is 10; negative powers mean reciprocals, never a logarithm approximation.

visuals.Title: Negative powers mean reciprocals
visuals.Description: Original exponent evaluation table. The nonzero base is 10; negative powers mean reciprocals, never a logarithm approximation.

visuals.Title: Positive and negative exponents of two
visuals.Description: Original exponent evaluation table. The nonzero base is 2; negative powers mean reciprocals, never a logarithm approximation.

visuals.Title: Decimal and scientific notation
visuals.Description: Scientific notation has a leading factor from 1 to below 10.

visuals.Title: Equally spaced small decimals
visuals.Description: Every number-line tick represents 0.0001, not 0.001.

visuals.Title: Scientific notation of 62,000
visuals.Description: 62000=6.2×10⁴ after moving the decimal four places.

visuals.Title: Add like powers of ten
visuals.Description: Both terms have scale 10⁵, so add coefficients: 3+2=5.

visuals.Title: Side length versus square area
visuals.Description: A square of edge s has area s².

visuals.Title: Doubling length quadruples square area
visuals.Description: From edge 2 to 4, area rises from 4 to 16, factor four.

visuals.Title: Exact right triangle triples
visuals.Description: Original right-triangle numeric verification of a²+b²=c². It supplements but does not replace a labeled proof diagram.

visuals.Title: Numerical decomposition for Pythagoras
visuals.Description: For a=3, b=4: outer square side 7 has area 49, four triangles total area 24, inner c²=25. This is NOT the actual visual proof.

visuals.Title: Determine unknown hypotenuses
visuals.Description: Original right-triangle numeric verification of a²+b²=c². It supplements but does not replace a labeled proof diagram.

visuals.Title: Shortest path after perpendicular travel
visuals.Description: Original right-triangle numeric verification of a²+b²=c². It supplements but does not replace a labeled proof diagram.

visuals.Title: Distance by coordinate differences
visuals.Description: From (−2,1) to (4,9), Δx=6 and Δy=8, so distance is 10. A coordinate grid is separately required.

visuals.Title: Cubic volume changes with edge length
visuals.Description: A cube with side length s has three equal dimensions and exact volume s³ cubic units.

visuals.Title: Real cube roots preserve negative signs
visuals.Description: Each cube root r satisfies r³=x even for negative x.

visuals.Title: Fill 360 degrees around a vertex
visuals.Description: Each indicated regular tile shape can meet without gaps when vertex angles sum to 360°.

visuals.Title: Hexagonal corners around a point
visuals.Description: Exactly three hexagon angles of 120° sum to 360°.

visuals.Title: Negative association with latitude
visuals.Description: Original lesson-example input-output table. Each row uses y = -0.5x + 40. Plotting this relation, when required, is a separate graphical task.

visuals.Title: Latitude as an input to a model
visuals.Description: Original lesson-example input-output table. Each row uses y = -0.5x + 40. Plotting this relation, when required, is a separate graphical task.

visuals.Title: Use a linear model without extrapolation claims
visuals.Description: Original lesson-example input-output table. Each row uses y = -0.5x + 40. Plotting this relation, when required, is a separate graphical task.
